text:
Anya: heads-up — we've got a customer reporting quota blowouts from streaming reconnects. they see ~2x tokens billed after a flaky mobile network. console counters don't match billing ledger. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

Sam: yes, saw similar in staging last week. root cause was double-counting of partial tokens when client reconnects and server re-sends last chunk. streaming path increments token counters on send, and resume path also replays without de-dupe.

Miguel: billing ledger counts every EVENT published to the token_ledger topic. platform realtime counters increment on send path, so if we replay a chunk we get two events unless we mark replay as replayed. mismatch is expected today.

Anya: example log from the customer (sanitized):
```
INFO stream=conn-7a token_chunk=chunk_42 tokens=18 sent=true
WARN stream=conn-7b replay_of=chunk_42 tokens=18 resent=true
```
Result: ledger shows +36 tokens across same API key in 12s.

Leila: two quick paths: 1) fix server dedupe (track last_ack per stream_id) 2) show 'tentative' usage in console while stream is open so users aren't surprised. UX idea: a small badge "tentative tokens: 120" and finalizes on stream close.

Sam: agree on server dedupe. implementation plan I sketched: add stream_resume_id header and a short LRU of (resume_id -> last_counted_offset) with TTL 5m. pseudocode:
```
# on send
if not seen(resume_id, offset): count_tokens(offset - last_offset); mark_seen(resume_id, offset)
else: skip_count()
```
Memory: about ~150k entries worst-case if lots of short-lived mobile clients, but we TTL aggressively.

Miguel: billing perspective — we need an authoritative event that says "finalized_tokens_for_stream" when stream is closed or when client acks resume. We can keep interim events for observability but mark them transient so they don't hit billing pipeline.

infra-bot: quota-bot triggered this alert: "high transient token delta for org: acme-tech". current enforcement behavior: per-key burst window consumed immediately on send. If we change counting semantics we must avoid letting users exceed hard burst limits during reconnect floods.

Sam: good point. proposal: enforce a conservative burst debit on initial send (tentative_debit) and move to committed debit only after stream confirmation or after a short confirmation window (e.g., 10s). If client reconnects and resumes within window, keep tentative as-is and avoid double-committing. If no confirmation, commit after window.

Anya: sounds reasonable. what's the operational complexity? can we do a toggle behind a feature-flag?

Leila: yes — implement server dedupe + tentative accounting + console UX as phased rollout. DEFAULT: old behavior. PHASE 1: enable tentative accounting per org for 10% traffic to validate telemetry. PHASE 2: switch default and expose org-level toggle in console.

Miguel: for auditability, ledger events should include these attributes (example event lines):
```
EVENT stream_chunk_transient {org:acme, key:abc, stream_id:conn-7a, resume_id:xyz, tokens:18}
EVENT stream_chunk_committed {org:acme, key:abc, stream_id:conn-7a, resume_id:xyz, tokens:18}
```
That way billing consumes only committed events.

Sam: client-side suggestion as fallback: client includes X-Resume-Token and X-Client-Ack headers on reconnect. server only re-sends chunks after client ack of last offset. example header usage:
```
POST /v1/streams/resume
Headers: Authorization, X-Resume-Token: abc123, X-Client-Ack: offset:42
```
If client doesn't ack, server can flag ambiguous and send conservative replays.

Anya: ops question — how will this interact with rate-limit enforcement path (per-key burst quotas)? we still need backpressure if a reconnect storm hits.

infra-bot: enforcement idea: require tentative debit to count against soft burst (allows queuing) and only commit to hard quota when committed event emitted. If commit would exceed hard quota, block the stream continuation and return 429 on resume. This gives protection while avoiding double-billing.

quota-bot: (automated) posting: "Quota policy updated? No, current policy: hard debit immediate. Proposed: tentative->commit flow. Will need update to /policies service and tests." :information_source:

Leila: telemetry changes needed: add resume_id to all stream metrics, add gauge for "tentative_tokens" and expose per-route breakdown in console. We'll need to update dashboards and alerts to use committed tokens for billing alerts and tentative for live-experience alerts.

Miguel: timeline suggestion: 1) small prototype (server dedupe + resume_id) 1 week 2) tentative accounting + telemetry + console UX 2-3 weeks 3) staged rollout + billing pipeline change 1 week + validation. total ~5 weeks.

Sam: I'll open a draft PR with the dedupe cache implementation and a feature-flag. putting <PR#1499> in the thread.

Anya: great. please add a small testkit harness that can simulate flaky reconnects and assert ledger vs console counts. also add a migration runbook for switching orgs.

Leila: I'll mock up a console badge and figma screens, will post later. :sparkles:

Miguel: one last note — ensure we keep exact replication for enterprise customers who want deterministic billing; option to opt-out of tentative accounting and keep strict immediate billing.

Sam: ack. I'll include an opt-out config per org.

Anya: thanks team. action items: Sam -> draft PR + tests; Leila -> console mock + telemetry spec; Miguel -> billing event contract; infra -> policy changes for quota service. follow up in #eng-platform sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
